analysis:
The change to docs/architecture/inference.md is documentation only. It adds a section (head lines ~3541-3575) describing how cluster service listeners follow the cable and the pairing. The two listeners are the setup exchange and the control lease. The section states that a listener is keyed to its pairing and refuses handshakes keyed to a later pairing, restarts when the cable port or address changes or the pairing changes, and stops when no pairing remains. It also says an unreadable pairing store changes nothing and that the pairing identity comparison excludes the edge secret. I examined only the base text excerpts in the supplied units and the patch excerpt, which is truncated; the base text (lines 3235-4002) is unchanged context. No code, configuration, endpoint or deployment change is in the supplied evidence.

No canonical threat IDs are materially affected. The text touches the experimental two-Mac cluster, which is outside TB-002, TB-011, T-041 and the other listed boundaries. The documented fail-closed handshake rejection on pairing mismatch is consistent with the existing pairing and authentication posture. Two integration questions remain unverified, because the source files (ClusterService.swift, ClusterSetupLinkExchange) were not supplied. First, whether the 5-second listener check and the 'restart without log' behaviour for the control lease listener could mask unexpected restarts; this is an observability point, not a vulnerability. Second, whether keeping an unreadable pairing store from changing a running listener leaves a stale pairing active until it is readable. Neither is a regression I can claim from docs alone.

The retained base content on the prefix cache, Flint and tensor-parallel probe files is unchanged and is not re-reviewed beyond orientation. Owner-only probe files and the other persisted histories are described as pre-existing.
